subject: Status update: elevated chunk-assembly lag causing short truncations on Hosted Generation (us-west)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medflow.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Observed streaming chunk assembly lag in us-west — immediate advisory

Carlos —

We observed an elevated rate of short truncations for streaming generation responses from our Hosted Generation endpoints in the us-west region starting ~08:50 PST. Affected behavior: customers using streaming endpoints may see occasional 1–4 token truncations at the end of chunks (it looks like chunk assembly is delayed and the last chunk closes early). Impact is intermittent (p95/99 spike) and affects both chat and stream APIs for longer outputs (>128 tokens).

What we’ve done so far:
- Triggered an ops bridge and engaged the runtime team to look for KV/cache assembly or batching regressions.
- Rolled a non-disruptive traffic routing rule to move a portion of traffic to an alternative us-west pool (no model changes).
- Published an initial notice on the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/usw-chunk-assembly-2028-01-12 (summary + mitigation steps).

Immediate asks for MedFlow: if you saw truncated responses, can you share 2–3 request ids and approximate timestamps (we already received one from your integration logs but more examples help triage). I’ve attached a short sample log and a status snapshot from 09:05.

Attachments: usw1_stream-sample-20280112.log, status_snapshot_usw1.png

We’ll follow up with an engineering update in ~2–3 hours. Apologies for the disruption — we realize streaming integrity is important for MedFlow’s real-time UI.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed streaming chunk assembly lag in us-west — immediate advisory

Hannah / team —

Quick updates from runtime:
- Root cause hypothesis: an upstream change to chunk assembly scheduling (recent queuing tweak) increased the probability of partial assembly for late-arriving token groups when tokens cross batching boundaries. We’re seeing elevated latch times on the assembler thread and a correlated bump in short-truncation telemetry.
- Short-term mitigation in place: the routing rule Hannah applied sends ~30% of traffic to a pool running the previous assembler config; that pool shows normal chunk latency in the metrics.
- Near-term fix: revert the scheduling tweak and deploy a safe guard that forces final-chunk completion for any active stream. We can push the revert as an incremental release within the next 2 hours; it’s low-risk.

I’ll prepare a test plan and hold a quick deploy window. If routing continues to show improvement, we can expand rollout.

Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medflow.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 13:32:00 -0800
Subject: Update: mitigation in place and planned revert — brief customer note

Carlos —

Quick customer-facing update: our engineering team identified a scheduling change that increased the chance of early chunk closure for late-arriving token groups. We have two mitigations active:

1) Traffic routing diversification — partial traffic moved to a stable pool (reduces observed truncations).
2) Planned revert — we will revert the scheduling change and deploy a guard that ensures final-chunk completion; deploy window planned for 15:10 PST today. Expected customer impact during the revert: a short (<5 minute) rolling push with no model changes; we do not anticipate further truncations after the revert.

If you have any scheduled demos today, let us know and we’ll coordinate timing. We appreciate the logs you sent — Marcus used them in the triage.

We will post the deployment note and an updated incident timeline on the status page immediately after the revert.

-Hannah
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jan 2028 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident review: scheduling + rollout guard (15 Jan 10:00 PST)

Team —

Thanks for the quick response on Friday. The revert completed as planned at 15:16 PST; preliminary telemetry looks good (truncation rate returned to baseline within ~10 minutes of completion).

I’ve scheduled a 60-minute post-incident review for Monday, 15 Jan at 10:00 PST to capture timeline, root cause, and action items (owner / ETA). Proposed agenda:
- Timeline and observable symptoms (5m)
- Root cause analysis (15m)
- Short/medium/long-term mitigations (20m)
- Customer communications + postmortem deliverables (10m)
- AOB and next steps (10m)

Please add notes to the draft doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2B_postmortem_medflow_usw. Marcus, please include the repro steps and the specific changelist for the scheduling tweak. Hannah, I’ll draft the external-facing postmortem after we align.

Laura
Director, Product Ops
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medflow.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Incident closed — postmortem & next steps (us-west streaming truncations)

Carlos —

We’re closing the incident and wanted to share the follow-up artifacts and next steps. Summary:
- Impact: intermittent 1–4 token truncations for streaming responses in us-west from ~08:50–15:16 PST on 12 Jan. Root cause: scheduling change to chunk assembly queuing that interacted poorly with late-arriving token groups crossing batching boundaries.
- Mitigation: routing diversion + scheduled revert deployed; truncation telemetry returned to baseline within ~10 minutes of the revert.
- Customer impact: brief user-visible truncations for a subset of long streaming requests — no data leakage or model changes.

Artifacts and next steps:
- Public incident page (live): https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/usw-chunk-assembly-2028-01-12
- Internal postmortem (draft): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2B_postmortem_medflow_usw (internal comments requested by EOD Wed 17 Jan).
- Planned follow-ups: add test coverage for late-arriving token groups, add a guard in the assembler that refuses to close a chunk unless finalization criteria are met, and include regression tests in the release pipeline (owners and ETAs will be documented in the postmortem).

If you’d like a short run-through of the postmortem findings for product/engineering stakeholders at MedFlow, I can schedule a 30-minute session this week. Again, apologies for the interruption — thanks for the patience and for the quick reproducer logs.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
